title: Give the ACCC a standing role championing competition in banking
action: Make the ACCC a permanent member of the Council of Financial Regulators with a mandate to champion competition, including in decisions by APRA and other regulators that may restrict it, and have APRA set capital risk weights for small business loans that better reflect their actual risk.
why: Prudential rules made without weighing their effect on competition can entrench the major banks; uniform risk weights make small business lending dearer than its risk justifies, especially from smaller lenders.

evidence.source: Competition in the Australian Financial System
evidence.quote: the ACCC should be given a mandate by the Australian Government to champion competition in the financial system, including in decisions taken by regulators that have or may have the outcome of restricting competition.

evidence.source: Competition in the Australian Financial System
evidence.quote: Instead of applying a single risk weight to all small and medium business lending not secured by a residence, APRA should provide for a broader schedule of risk weights in its Australian Prudential Standard (APS 112).
